text:
Done — the habit tracker is built, and I drove it end to end rather than trusting the graph.

## What's there

`/private/tmp/claude-501/.../scratchpad/d-kit-1/work/apps/habit-tracker` — a NodeGX app, four components:

- **`Pages/Home`** — the whole app: title and today's date, "2 of 3 done today", a field + **Add**, then one card per habit.
- **`Components/HabitRow`** — a habit's card: name, a streak pill, the last 7 days as seven marks, **Mark done today / Done today** (with a check glyph), and a quiet **Delete** at the far end of the row.
- **`Components/DayMark`** — one day: a square with the weekday letter, filled when done, ringed when it's today. No code in it at all.
- One **Function** ("the store") owns the habits — `localStorage`, one key, written whole on every change.

## What I actually verified (not just wired)

`validate_project`: **0 errors, 0 warnings** across 48 nodes / 92 endpoints. Then I pressed through it in a real browser, twice (desktop 1280 and phone 390):

- add a habit → appears; tick today → the mark fills, the button says **Done today**, the summary moves to `1 of 1 done today`
- **reload** → still ticked, still there, streak shows `1 day in a row`
- untick → back to `Mark done today`, `No streak yet`; **Delete** → the card goes, the empty state returns
- edges: a duplicate name disables **Add** and shows a hint; a name containing a colon (`Read: 10 pages`) saves correctly; a whitespace-only name adds nothing; no console errors anywhere

One thing worth telling you because it's the kind of bug that ships silently: a habit row **cannot** hand a value up through the Repeater — its item output is only filled as part of the Repeater's own action flow. I measured that (the row committed `set:h1:1` while the page side stayed empty) and moved the row→page hop onto a shared `habit-command` variable. That, and everything else I decided, is written down in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

## Open it

```
npx @nodegx/preview /private/tmp/claude-501/.../work/apps/habit-tracker --open
```

For your phone on the same Wi-Fi, add `--host 0.0.0.0` and open the address it prints. (NodeGX Studio isn't installed on this machine, so that command is how you look at it; the app also opens again this way another day.)

## Three choices you may want to change

- **A streak survives an unticked morning** — it counts back from today, or from yesterday while today is still unticked, so it only breaks when a whole day is missed. (I'd rather that than seeing `0` at breakfast.)
- **Names are unique** — adding a name you already have is refused, with the reason shown under the field. This is what makes the Add button safe; without it, a second press carrying the same string is indistinguishable from the first.
- **Delete is one press, no confirmation.** It takes the habit's history with it. Say the word and I'll add a confirm or an undo.

Also not built (all listed as `> TODO:` in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`): renaming a habit, a Monday–Sunday window instead of the 7 days ending today, and history beyond 7 days.

The project is yours: a folder of files on your computer, with the decisions and the reasons in `docs/` (including what I rejected — a backend, per-day tick records, a date library). A few screenshots from the build are in `.previews/`; delete the folder whenever you like. If Studio is more than you want, ask me for an editor built for how you think about this app — and the one part it can't edit is the store Function's script and the little expressions beside it; Studio shows you what they produce and lets you look at the wiring underneath.

To come back: ask for reminders, a weekly view, or an export of your ticks.
